articles.headline: The 2028 O'Reilly Auto Parts Series Silly Season Shakes Up the Garage
articles.dek: Fresh faces and high-profile ladder moves headline the garage as the 2028 O'Reilly Auto Parts Series prepares to take the green flag.
articles.body:
The offseason garage shuffle is officially in the books, and the 2028 NASCAR O'Reilly Auto Parts Series grid looks entirely overhauled before a single lap has been turned. Silly season delivered massive changes up and down the pit lane, setting up a fascinating dynamic for the year ahead.

Noah Gragson anchors the biggest veteran shift, dropping down to the O'Reilly Auto Parts Series to pilot the Peterson Racing number 87 machine after departing Front Row Motorsports. Gragson brings instant Cup-level pedigree to the Peterson operation, immediately elevating expectations for the team as the new season looms.

Meanwhile, the ladder system continues to churn out top-tier talent. Layne Riggs steps up to the O'Reilly Auto Parts Series to take over the Hendrick Motorsports number 17 ride, transitioning over from Front Row Motorsports. Joining him in the series influx is Gio Ruggiero, who makes the jump from Tricon Garage to wheel the JR Motorsports number 8 machine.

Upward mobility defined the rest of the major offseason moves. Sammy Smith departs JR Motorsports to move up to the Cup Series with Kaulig Racing in the number 16. Corey Day also makes the leap to the premier level, leaving Hendrick Motorsports to drive the number 4 for Front Row Motorsports. With the grid finalized, attention now turns to the season opener to see how these new manufacturer and team pairings perform under pressure.
articles.author: Marcy Teague
